text: It flew over a truck and hung upside down.
This October, Tesla drove its new Roadster up a curved ramp and stopped.
Every square meter around you carries about tons of air.
– roughly two elephants. But the Roadster's four fans suck the air out from under it.
Less air below, same air outside. So the air pins it to the road, even upside down.
How hard? Tesla claims about 4,700 kilograms – nearly three times the car's weight.
But Tesla didn't invent this. Rewind to 1978. A Formula One car raced in Sweden with
a giant fan on its back.
It's for cooling the engine, honest.
It won its only race by over half a minute.
So the Roadster isn't beating gravity, it's turning the sky against it.
Ten thrusters, built with SpaceX, blast out 600 liters of squeezed air.
It hopped over five Teslas, rolled in mid-air, and landed.
